Keep a copy of the declaration of entitlement to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay made by your employee. You may need to record this as evidence for subsequent periods of Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay.

Employee taken into legal custody

You cannot pay Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay for any week your employee is in legal custody or for any week in the pay period after that. You must give them the non-payment of Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay form.

Keep a copy of the declaration of entitlement to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay made by your employee. You may need to record this as evidence for subsequent periods of Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay.

It’s your employee’s responsibility to tell you if they are taken into legal custody. Your employee is in legal custody if they are detained. Usually this means they are arrested or in prison.

They are not in legal custody if they are:

voluntarily helping police with their enquiries

out on bail

serving a suspended sentence

Changes for employees employed in Northern Ireland from 6 April 2026

Earnings affected by a backdated pay rise for employees employed in Northern Ireland

From 6 April 2026 if your employee was not entitled to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay based on either:

their actual earnings in the qualifying period before the pay rise

the initial calculation used all or partly expected earnings

You must recalculate their average weekly earnings.

You can then check if they may now be entitled to the pay or an increased amount of payment in line with the backdated pay amounts and pay any Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay due.

If the employee now qualifies based on actual earning in the recalculation, you must pay any Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay the employee is now entitled to. You need to record the updated amount in your own records and update any relevant EPS or by submitting FPS where a change occurs.

Salary sacrifice

From 6 April 2026, for an employee employed in Northern Ireland with a salary sacrifice, you should calculate their average weekly earnings using actual, expected, or combined figures during the qualifying earnings period.

Miscarriage for employees in Northern Ireland

From the 6 April 2026 an employee employed in Northern Ireland will be entitled to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay when:

the employee has experienced a miscarriage and has become aware of it

they are a person who has a connection or is in a relationship with the woman who has experienced the miscarriage

The 56 week qualifying period will begin when the woman who has experienced the miscarriage has become aware of it.

More than one miscarriage

The employee can claim 2 weeks Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay for each miscarriage that occurs. There is no limit on how many claims the employee can make.

Employee leaves job before Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay is taken — Northern Ireland

If your employee has left their job, they cannot get parental bereavement leave. If they left:

before the date of the child’s death, stillbirth or the woman who experienced the miscarriage first became aware of the miscarriage, they are not entitled to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay

after the date of the child’s death, stillbirth or the woman who experienced the miscarriage first became aware of the miscarriage, they may be entitled to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay

If your employee left after the child’s date of death, stillbirth or the woman who experienced the miscarriage first became aware of the miscarriage, it does not matter why they left or that they’re not coming back. They’re entitled to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay as long as they do not work for a new employer during the week in which Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay is being claimed.

If the employment ends after the child dies or is stillborn or the woman who experienced the miscarriage first became aware of the miscarriage, but before the planned start of the Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay period, you may treat the Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay period as beginning on the day after the last day of employment.

Your employee may choose when to begin their Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay period on or after the date of death, but the period must end within 56 weeks of the date of death, or the date that the woman who experienced the miscarriage became aware of the miscarriage.

Reinstatement and employment after a break in employment

For employees in Northern Ireland, the rules for Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay are different where eligibility is gained on or after 6 April 2026

If an employee gains eligibility on or after this date, including someone who has been reinstated or who has returned after a break in employment, they will be entitled to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay as long as they were employed by you (or deemed reinstated after dismissal) on the date:

of the child’s death

of the stillbirth

the woman who experienced the miscarriage became aware of it

To assess their earnings for eligibility, the employee can use the following over a continuous 8‑week period:

their normal weekly earnings

their expected earnings

a combination of both

Reinstatement after dismissal

Your employee is entitled to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay (as if they had not been dismissed) if they did not work for you because you dismissed them and the bereavement occurred before or during the period dismissal, and either:

they are then reinstated because an employment tribunal decides that you dismissed them unfairly

you reinstate them as a result of a statutory grievance procedure

All the other conditions to entitlement must be satisfied.

Parental bereavement leave is a day one right.
